DEV-10 is done and In Review, with all four points met.

- **Fix:** the bug was in `_get_search_url`. It checked whether the word left after the engine name was itself an engine name, so `test path-search` opened the `path-search` engine's homepage. Now only a single bare engine name, with `open_base_url` on, opens a homepage; any multi-word entry is a normal search.
- **Regression test:** the `test path-search` case runs with `open_base_url` on and off, plus two more tests in `test_urlutils.py`. On the old code, two of the new cases fail.
- **Existing tests:** `test_urlutils.py` gives 247 passed, 1 skipped. The full `tests/unit/utils/` run still fails 21 tests, but the untouched commit fails the same 21. They come from the newer Python/PyQt in the venv, not the patch. The team agreed to count point 2 as met when that list stays exactly the same.
- **`final.patch`:** Dev C attached it with the test output, and it applies cleanly with `git apply` to a fresh `a55f4db26`. It is Dev B's patch, approved by me and Dev D, plus a one-space indent fix that flake8 would have flagged.
- **Not run:** flake8, pylint and mypy aren't installed and there's no internet access, so line lengths and whitespace were only checked by hand.

There's one deliberate behaviour change for you to accept or reject when merging. With `auto_search=never` and `open_base_url` on, typing only an engine name now opens that engine's homepage instead of being treated as a web address. That is what the option is documented to do, and it's covered by a test and a changelog line. Dev B's comment with `candidate.patch` gives the one-line change to keep the old behaviour.

I posted a short confirmation on the issue after checking `final.patch` myself. My scratch checkouts are removed and `~/work/qutebrowser` is back to clean on `work`.

**Still running:** your reminder wakeups keep starting short runs after every finished run until each hits its 20-run limit. Agents can't turn them off ("permission denied"), so the thread is full of one-line "no change" comments, and more will follow. Only you can turn the reminders off.
